project-charter.title: Project Charter

cards.title: Real-World Industrial Scenario
cards.body: At Kirloskar Pump Systems, Pune, an industrial centrifugal water pumping system is driven by a 22 kW three-phase electric motor operating at 1440 rpm. Power is delivered from the motor output shaft (diameter d = 40 mm) to the centrifugal pump input shaft via an inline mechanical coupling connection. Pumping operations involve continuous fluid delivery under fluctuating pressure heads, exposing the drive train to light shock loads, minor alignment shifts, and cyclic torque fluctuations. As a Senior Mechanical Design Engineer, your task is to evaluate the power transmission requirements, analyze component identification on Engineering Asset EA-09, classify coupling types, calculate transmitted torque, select the optimal coupling, and provide rigorous engineering justification.

cards.title: Role & Assignment Scope
cards.body: As a Mechanical Design Engineer, you must investigate shaft connection mechanics, shaft alignment tolerances, torque transmission, shock/vibration damping, space constraints, and serviceability. You will determine transmitted torque T and design torque Td, evaluate rigid vs flexible coupling characteristics, select the most appropriate coupling, and formulate an evidence-based technical decision.

engineering-context.title: Engineering Context

cards.title: Shaft Connection & Alignment Mechanics
cards.body: In power transmission systems, connecting driving and driven machines using a single continuous rigid shaft is impractical due to manufacturing limitations, installation tolerances, thermal expansion, foundation settling, and maintenance requirements. Mechanical couplings serve as essential machine elements that connect two coaxial shafts end-to-end to transmit torque while accommodating allowable shaft misalignments (radial/parallel, angular, and axial) and damping torsional shock and vibration.

working-principle.title: Working Principle
working-principle.prompt: Explain the mechanical torque transmission path from the electric motor to the pump impeller and describe how flexible coupling elements accommodate shaft misalignment.

mcq.question: What is the primary mechanical function of the elastomeric flexible element (bushes or spider) in a flexible coupling?
options: To permanently lock the two shafts rigidly together without any relative motion
To transmit torque while absorbing torsional shock loads and accommodating slight shaft misalignments
To increase the rotational speed of the driven pump shaft relative to the motor shaft
To eliminate the need for keys and keyways on driving and driven shafts
mcq.answer: To transmit torque while absorbing torsional shock loads and accommodating slight shaft misalignments

coupling-classification.title: Classification of Couplings
coupling-classification.prompt: Classify couplings into Rigid and Flexible categories according to standard machine design principles.

options.title: Rigid Flange Coupling
options.description: Consists of two heavy cast iron flanged hubs keyed to shafts and bolted tightly together. Requires perfect coaxial alignment; cannot accommodate any axial, radial, or angular misalignment.

options.title: Bushed-Pin Flexible Coupling
options.description: Modification of rigid flange coupling using steel pins covered with flexible rubber bushes fitted into hub sockets. Transmits torque, accommodates slight misalignment, and absorbs shock.

options.title: Oldham Coupling
options.description: Features two outer hubs with radial slots and a central floating disc with perpendicular tongues. Specifically designed to connect shafts having lateral (parallel) offset misalignment.

options.title: Gear Coupling
options.description: Consists of external crowned gear teeth on hubs mating with internal spur gear teeth in a sleeve. High torque capacity, accommodates angular and axial misalignment, requires grease lubrication.

options.title: Elastomeric Jaw / Spider Coupling
options.description: Uses two interlocking metallic jaw hubs separated by an elastomeric spider element. Failsafe design, easy inspection, dampens high-frequency vibration, suitable for small to medium power.

application-analysis.title: Application Analysis
application-analysis.prompt: Analyze real-world industrial drive applications and determine the governing coupling requirements for each scenario.

options.title: Electric Motor to Centrifugal Water Pump (22 kW, 1440 rpm)
options.requirements: Medium torque, continuous duty, slight thermal expansion & mounting misalignment, low-to-medium shock loading, ease of maintenance without disturbing motor/pump setup.

options.title: Heavy Duty Reciprocating Air Compressor Drive
options.requirements: High cyclic torque peaks, severe pulsating shock loads, significant torsional vibration, requiring heavy shock damping and high torsional flexibility.

options.title: Mining Belt Conveyor Reducer Drive
options.requirements: Very high starting torque, heavy overloads, severe dust and moisture environment, requiring overload protection and rugged metallic flexibility.

options.title: Precision CNC Machine Tool Lead Screw Drive
options.requirements: Zero backlash, high positional accuracy, low torque, exact angular synchronization, requiring torsionally rigid yet flexible bellows or Oldham coupling.

coupling-comparison.title: Coupling Comparison
coupling-comparison.prompt: Compare Rigid Flange, Bushed-Pin Flexible, Oldham, Gear, and Elastomeric Spider couplings across critical engineering performance parameters.

options.title: Rigidity & Alignment Requirement
options.comparison: Rigid Flange requires zero shaft misalignment (<0.02 mm). Flexible couplings (Bushed-Pin, Gear, Spider) tolerate 0.5° angular and 0.5-1.5 mm axial/parallel misalignments without excessive bearing loads.

options.title: Shock Absorption & Vibration Damping
options.comparison: Rigid Flange provides 0% shock absorption. Bushed-Pin and Elastomeric Spider couplings provide excellent shock damping (20-35% reduction in peak torque transfers) due to resilient rubber inserts.

options.title: Maintenance & Replacement Convenience
options.comparison: Bushed-Pin and Elastomeric Spider couplings allow replacement of worn rubber bushes/spider elements without axially shifting or disturbing the motor or pump heavy castings.

options.title: Economic Practicality & Availability
options.comparison: Bushed-Pin flexible couplings offer the optimal balance of low initial cost, standard availability across Indian industrial suppliers (SPPU/Kirloskar standards), and minimal maintenance.

coupling-selection.title: Coupling Selection
coupling-selection.prompt: Select the most suitable coupling type for connecting the 22 kW, 1440 rpm electric motor shaft (d = 40 mm) to the centrifugal pump input shaft.

options.title: Rigid Flange Coupling
options.reason: Cannot accommodate even minor operational shaft misalignments or thermal expansion; risks severe bending stresses and early bearing failure.

options.title: Bushed-Pin Flexible Coupling (RECOMMENDED)
options.reason: Excellently transmits Td = 218.83 N-m, accommodates minor parallel and angular misalignments, absorbs pump shock loads, allows easy bush replacement without unbolting motor/pump.

options.title: Oldham Coupling
options.reason: Designed specifically for large parallel offset misalignments at low speeds; excessive sliding friction and wear under continuous 1440 rpm pump operation.

options.title: Gear Coupling
options.reason: Suitable for heavy industrial steel mills requiring extreme torque; unnecessarily complex, expensive, and requires periodic grease lubrication for a standard 22 kW pump.

engineering-justification.title: Engineering Justification
engineering-justification.prompt: Provide technical engineering justification supporting your selection of the Bushed-Pin Flexible Coupling for the motor-pump power transmission system.
options: Torque Capacity — Safely transmits design torque Td = 218,838 N-mm with Kl = 1.5 service factor
Misalignment Accommodation — Rubber bushes absorb axial (0.5-1.5 mm), parallel (0.5 mm), and angular (0.5 deg) shaft misalignments
Shock & Vibration Damping — Elastomeric inserts isolate high-frequency pump vibrations and protect motor/pump bearings
Maintenance & Serviceability — Worn rubber bushes are easily replaced without moving heavy motor or pump castings
Economic Practicality — Standard Indian industrial availability (SPPU/Kirloskar standards) with low initial and maintenance costs

engineering-decision.title: Engineering Decision & Alternative Analysis
engineering-decision.prompt: Summarize your final engineering decision, specifying the chosen coupling, application parameters, technical justification, alternative coupling evaluated, and why the alternative was rejected.
options: RECOMMENDED: Bushed-Pin Flexible Coupling (Optimal selection for 22 kW motor to centrifugal pump drive)
REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: Rigid Flange Coupling (Cannot accommodate shaft misalignment; risks early bearing failure)
REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: Oldham Coupling (Excessive sliding wear and friction at 1440 rpm continuous speed)
REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: Gear Coupling (Over-engineered, expensive, and requires continuous grease lubrication)
